title: RuneScape Dragonwilds Update v1.0.1 Patch Notes - Save Fixes, New Attacks & MASSIVE Bug Fixes!
author: NRS NEO
description:
RuneScape: Dragonwilds just received its biggest update yet, released on October 14! 🔥 This update brings major improvements, new combat abilities, expanded inventory space, equipment changes, and a massive wave of bug fixes.

The update focuses on fixing disappearing world saves and introduces a recovery option for corrupted character saves, helping affected players get back into the action with aggregated stats and Tier 4 gear.

There is plenty more to check out, including the new Death From Above jump attack, unique special attacks for shortbows, longbows, and crossbows, Ammo Recovery perks, and the new Low Blow ability. Inventory space has increased from 32 to 40 slots, while dedicated ring and amulet slots make equipment management more convenient.

You'll also find improved item sorting, a Completed Quests tab, new composting options, enemy behaviour adjustments, and fixes covering multiplayer, bosses, crafting, performance, controls, visuals, and much more.

In this video, we go through the major additions, gameplay improvements, and important fixes included in this update.

What you'll find in this update:
🔥 Disappearing save fixes and character recovery
⚔️ New Death From Above attack
🏹 New shortbow, longbow, and crossbow special attacks
🎒 Inventory expanded to 40 slots
💍 Dedicated ring and amulet slots
📜 Completed Quests tab and improved sorting
🐉 Boss, combat, and multiplayer bug fixes
🛠️ Performance, UI, crafting, and exploration improvements

#RuneScapeDragonwilds

transcript.text: Hey, what's going on, guys? My name is Nico Russell, and this is the biggest update released on RuneScape Dragon Wild
so far, released on October 14th. The first major improvement is all about save files.
Some players have been reporting that their world saves were disappearing, which is obviously a pretty serious
problem when you've spent hours gathering resources, building your base, upgrading your equipment, and exploring
new regions. Um this update introduces a range of fixes aimed at those missing world saves. There's also a recovery
mechanic for corrupted character saves. Instead of leaving affected players to start again with nothing, the recovery
option gives them aggregated stats and tier four gear, so they can get back into the action without having to
rebuild their entire character from the beginning. Now, um the developers have pointed out that
there may still be some other save problems affecting a very limited number of players, and they are continuing to
investigate those cases. So, this is a meaningful step forward, although it may not resolve every
possible save issue just yet. Moving on to combat, we have a brand new attack that melee players are probably
going to enjoy. It's called death from above, and you unlock it through the skill tree. Uh once you've got the perk,
being high enough above the ground beyond the maximum height of a regular double jump allows you to attack while
airborne and slam down onto enemies below. Your damage depends on the weapon you're currently holding, which means your
choice of equipment still matters when setting up the attack. And here's a nice detail. Wind Step
works with it, too. That opens up some interesting ways to approach a fight, especially if you
enjoy using movement abilities to get above your enemies before coming down with a powerful hit. Rather than just
jumping around to avoid attacks, you can now turn that height advantage into actual damage.
Ranged combat is getting some attention, as well, and this is one of my favorite parts of the update because bows and
crossbows now have more distinct special attacks. There are also two new skill perks, ammo
recovery and greater ammo recovery. Um these give you a chance to recover arrows from defeated enemies, which
should help reduce the number of arrows you need to craft or carry when you're spending a long time away from your base.
The short bow gets rapid fire. When you activate it, your character hops backwards and fires three arrows in
quick succession. You can even switch targets between shots, so you're not locked into
attacking one enemy the entire time. Um that makes it useful when several enemies are approaching and you need to
spread the damage around. The long bow gets power shot, which takes a different approach. Your
character kneels down, draws an arrow at full strength, and releases a powerful shot that can travel a long distance.
This should be particularly useful when you want to hit a dangerous enemy before it gets close enough to attack you.
Then there's the crossbow, which receives heavy bolt. You charge the attack briefly before
firing a powerful bolt, and the shot also applies enchanted effects when it hits. That added effect makes it worth
considering when you're dealing with enemies that are vulnerable to those abilities.
Ranged players also get a perk called low blow. When your ranged attack hits an enemy in
the legs or the lower third of its body, it applies hamstring, reducing the target's movement speed for a short time.
That could make it easier to keep your distance while dealing damage. There are exceptions, though.
Tiny and colossal enemies are immune, so this isn't going to slow down absolutely everything you encounter.
There's also an ammunition balance change worth mentioning. Rune arrows and rune bolts now deal more
damage than their adamant counterparts, with the listed damage multipliers moving to 4.9 compared with 4.2.
So, if you've been investing in higher tier ammunition, there is now a better damage advantage to go along with that
investment. Now, let's talk about inventory management because this is one of those changes you'll probably appreciate
almost immediately. Your inventory has increased from 32 slots to 40. That gives you more room for resources,
crafting materials, food, ammunition, and whatever else you tend to collect while exploring. Anyone who regularly
has to stop and decide which items to leave behind should notice the difference. Equipment management is
improving, too, with dedicated slots for both rings and amulets. You no longer have to treat those
accessories as though they're competing for the same equipment space. It's a welcome addition, especially for
players who enjoy working on their character build and combining different bonuses. There is one balance adjustment
alongside this change. The Amulet of Glory was providing more bonuses than intended, so its effects have been
reduced to bring it closer to the intended balance. The sorting options have also been improved.
Sorting by weight now considers the combined weight of each item stack and places the heaviest first.
Type groups items into categories arranged alphabetically, while latest puts your most recently collected items
first. These sound like basic inventory features, but when you're carrying dozens of different resources, being
able to find the right thing without manually searching through everything makes a real difference.
Quest tracking gets an improvement as well. There is now a completed quests tab, including a short summary of how
each quest ended. That gives you a convenient way to review finished quests and remember their outcomes without
having to rely entirely on your memory. For anyone who likes following the story alongside exploration and progression,
this should be a useful addition. Crafting and farming receive a few changes, too. We now have the ultra compost bin and
the large compost bucket, with the bucket offering a greater capacity. Overdrive can also be cast on the
advanced spinning wheel, opening up another option for processing resources. The fishing cape perk now displays
correctly, including its chance to instantly catch a fish. Um, these aren't the biggest combat
changes in the update, but they add some welcome improvements to everyday activities.
Exploration and enemy behavior have been adjusted in a couple of useful ways. Enemy aggro ranges have been reduced
across the game, so you should be less likely to attract a whole group of enemies from far away and end up
fighting an unwanted parade of creatures. Uh, enemy respawn timers have also been
extended, meaning defeated enemies stay gone for longer while you move through an area. That should make exploring
certain locations feel less hectic, especially when you gather materials or focus on a particular objective.
The Scorned Wilderness raid has also received an adjustment. Obstacles and enemies now respawn when
the raid resets or when you return for another run. Mining nodes across the world have
received a polished pass to ensure they're positioned above ground and can actually be mined. There was even a fix
for players trying to open the map while mounted, along with improvements to the ambient goblin sounds.
Yes, even the goblins should should sound a little less like they're shouting the moment they notice you.
There is also a setting to toggle the visceral attack camera change, which gives players more control over that
particular combat effect. On the control side, several key bindings that could cause the player to
become stuck in certain situations can no longer be reassigned. These include interaction, building
actions, spell removal, crafting navigation, and quest dialogue options. It's a practical restriction designed to
prevent control setups that could leave you unable to perform an essential action. And then we get to the enormous
collection of bug fixes, covering progression, multiplayer, bosses, magic, performance, visuals, audio, and
interface problems. One particularly important fix addresses quest items obtained early through multiplayer sessions.
Previously, acquiring certain items ahead of the intended progression could prevent players from entering the next
region. Emaru's Head was one example, with players finding themselves unable to enter Fel Hollow. Um that progression
problem has now been addressed. There are fixes for online play, too. Players could encounter a crash when
selecting after being in offline mode, and that issue has been resolved. Dedicated server support has also
received attention, including a fix for players using the Epic Games Store who couldn't view dedicated servers, even
after previously connecting to them. On dedicated servers, um players should also be able to place
foundations and floor pieces in locations where those structures had previously been destroyed.
A number of combat and boss issues have been corrected. Enfeeble now reduces damage more effectively across enemy types.
Some enemies that weren't responding properly to enchanted iron bolts should now receive the intended effect.
And Titan's Wrath no longer sets the player on fire when its special attack is used repeatedly in quick succession.
There are also fixes for inaccurate damage against blue dragons when fighting from different heights,
troublesome camera lock-on behavior inside cultures interior, and a problem that could make Fuzon become passive or
effectively invisible after certain player deaths. Performance has received attention, as well.
One issue involving luring the black dragon into a safe spot could cause performance drops on some hardware,
while placing a personal chest near certain items could produce a large hitch or freeze. Both have been addressed.
There are also fixes for green dragons getting caught on the edges of an instance area, a brief freeze when
dismounting for the first time after launch, and various other situations where the game behaved unexpectedly.
The visual and interface fixes cover a surprising number of details. Rain effects should no longer appear inside
player housing. UI scaling is now available across all platforms as intended, and inventory tooltips should
display correctly on Xbox and PC. Controller users also get fixes for chest sorting and directional
navigation, while range special attacks should now trigger gamepad vibration properly.
Other corrections deal with map fog, skill menu navigation, misplaced visual effects, incorrectly displayed status
icons, and audio that wasn't playing at the right time. Some particularly specific problems have
been fixed, too, including a rune spade appearing upside down on a weapons rack, and a dragon med helm icon showing the
wrong shade of red. There are also fixes for freezing keyboards after teleporting, misplaced journal images, and several
issues involving crafting stations, farming plots, spells, and building menus. Achievements have received attention,
including issues affecting regicide, strike true, and the gilded gyrfalcon amulet reward.
Certain rewards and skill effects should now unlock or activate as intended, which is important for players working
through longer progression goals. The developers have also confirmed that their plans extend beyond this update,
with a roadmap plan for 2027 and the blood crystal saga on the way. Um those are future plans rather than
features arriving with this patch, but they show that more changes are planned for the months ahead.
So, overall, this update covers a lot more than adding a few attacks and increasing inventory space.
There are new ways to approach combat, better options for managing equipment, improvements to quest tracking,
adjustments to enemy behavior, and a huge range of fixes that address problems players could encounter during
exploration, crafting, boss fights, and multiplayer sessions. The save recovery work is
especially because losing progress can affect everything else you've been working towards.
Add in the expanded inventory, dedicated accessory slots, and more varied ranged attacks, and there's quite a lot here
for different types of players to appreciate.
